key_insight: SPHERE turns VR scene generation into a continuous co-creation loop by learning a user's spatial preferences from speech and controller edits, then adapting future layouts with human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning.
engineering_relevance: The framework is relevant for immersive design tools because it can reduce repetitive corrective editing and physical fatigue while preserving user-specific layout preferences across sessions.
method: Extracts persistent preferences from multimodal VR interactions (speech + controller edits).
Converts raw edits into hierarchical spatial constraints capturing local function and global topology.
Uses human-in-the-loop RL to update retrieval policies from the user's final edited scenes.
evidence_signal: A mixed-design user study with 42 participants plus offline ablations show fewer corrective edits and lower physical demand, while improving alignment to user profiles and geometric resilience.
watch_item: The approach may depend on high-quality interaction traces and careful policy updates to avoid overfitting to shallow object-level preferences or noisy edits.
paper_title: SPHERE: Adaptive VR Indoor Scene Generation via LLM-Enhanced Spatial Preference Learning and Human-in-the-Loop RL
